review: The hymn is the prayer for the shining face: 1:1 is the title-line and 2:1 repeats it verbatim, as the print does; 2:2–4 is Ps 27:1 with Num 6:26, 3:1–4 is Exod 33:18–19 (הַרְאֵנִי נָא אֶת־כְּבֹדֶךָ) with Ps 22:19, and 4:1–4 is Ps 4:7 with Ps 44:16, and 5:1–4 is Heb 4:16 (כִּסֵּא הַחֶסֶד) with Ps 118:8–9.

Stanza 1 is a single printed line, the theme of the hymn set on its own before the stanzas begin; the payload keeps it as one line and does not merge it with stanza 2, so the printed 1/4/4/4/4 shape survives.

3:3 קְרָא־נָא שֵׁם אֲדֹנָי לְפָנַי — the Arabic نَادِ بِاسْمِ الرَّبِّ قُدَّامِي is 'proclaim the Lord's name before me'; the Hebrew keeps the imperative and the tetragrammaton-substitute אֲדֹנָי, because the line is the Exod 33:19 proclamation (וַיִּקְרָא בְּשֵׁם יְהוָה) and not a general invocation.

4:3 הַמַּכְלִים צוֹרְרָי — the Arabic الَّذِي يُخْزِي الْأَعَادِي is 'which shames the foes'; the Hebrew uses כָּלַם, the verb of Ps 44:8 and Isa 41:11 for the shaming of enemies, so the line keeps the psalm's judicial shame and not merely defeat.
